subtitle: Warrior of Vatapi, Servant of Siva

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a lone commander before a distant fortified city
panels.action: Paranjothi Siruthondar stands in Pallava war-gear on a rocky rise, sword lowered, gaze steady toward the far silhouette of Vatapi’s walls under a heavy Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: In the age of Narasimhavarman, when Pallava banners rode to Vatapi, a general named Paranjothi would one day be remembered as Siruthondar, a warrior counted among Siva’s saints.

i18n.hi: नरसिंहवर्मन के समय, जब पल्लव ध्वजाएँ वातापि तक गईं, परञ्जोति नाम का एक सेनापति बाद में सिरुथोंदार कहलाया, शिव के वीर संतों में गिना गया।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Kanchipuram’s temples and royal quarters at dawn
panels.action: Paranjothi walks along the outer street of a Kanchipuram temple, his military cloak over simple garments, watching priests and common folk move in morning devotion near sculpted shrines.

dialogue.text: Kanchipuram, Pallava capital, was both fortress and holy city. Here generals walked beneath temple towers, where kings listened to brahmins and poets sang of Siva in the Tamil tongue.

i18n.hi: कांचीपुरम, पल्लव राजधानी, किला भी थी और पवित्र नगर भी। यहाँ सेनापति मंदिर-शिखरों के नीचे चलते, राजा ब्राह्मणों की सुनते और कवि तमिल में शिव का गान करते।

panels.shot: medium shot, side profile, Paranjothi in audience hall with implied king unseen
panels.action: Paranjothi stands upright in a pillared hall, hand to chest in respectful salute, as unseen royals and ministers in the shadows confer, palm-leaf maps and miniature models of fort walls laid before them.

dialogue.text: From inscriptions we know a Pallava host marched against Vatapi, Chalukya stronghold. Tradition places Paranjothi there, a commander trusted to carry Narasimhavarman’s will to the western hills.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख बताते हैं कि पल्लव सेना वातापि, चालुक्य गढ़, पर चढ़ी। परम्परा कहती है कि परञ्जोति वहीं थे, सेनानायक जिन्हें नरसिंहवर्मन की आज्ञा पश्चिमी पहाड़ियों तक पहुँचाने का भरोसा था।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye of Pallava army snaking across dry plains
panels.action: Paranjothi rides at the front of a long column of infantry, cavalry and elephants moving over dusty terrain, banners fluttering, spearheads catching harsh sunlight as the land stretches toward rocky outcrops.

dialogue.text: Armies moved with dust and iron, pushing north and west. The Kuram plates preserve the memory of this Vatapi campaign, when Pallava strength answered old rivalry with the Chalukyas.

i18n.hi: सेनाएँ धूल और लोहे के साथ उत्तर-पश्चिम बढ़ती रहीं। कुरम ताम्रपट्ट यह वातापि अभियान याद रखते हैं, जब पल्लव शक्ति ने चालुक्यों से पुरानी दुश्मनी का जवाब दिया।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-wide of Vatapi’s rocky hill fort under siege
panels.action: From a vantage outside the walls, Paranjothi watches siege engines and ranks of archers arrayed before Vatapi’s hill fort, layered defences looming above; smoke hangs thinly as the sun lowers.

dialogue.text: Vatapi’s walls rose from rock, layered with bastions and gates. The clash here would decide power between Kanchi and Badami, reshaping the balance along the Deccan plateau.

i18n.hi: वातापि की दीवारें चट्टान से उठती थीं, बुर्जों और फाटकों से परतदार। यहीं की टक्कर तय करती कि ताकत कांची और बादामी में किसकी रहे, दक्कन की धरती पर संतुलन बदलने वाली।

panels.shot: close shot of Paranjothi on the field, face set, yet contemplative
panels.action: Paranjothi sits briefly on a stone amid the outer camp, helmet off, hair tied back, fingers resting on his sword hilt as he gazes toward a small portable shrine to Siva lit by a single oil lamp.

dialogue.text: War needed discipline, clear command, hardened nerve. Yet many who bore arms also bore devotion. In later memory, Paranjothi’s steel and his service to Siva became one.

i18n.hi: युद्ध को अनुशासन, साफ़ आज्ञा, मजबूत मन चाहिए। पर कई योद्धा भक्ति भी ढोते थे। बाद की याद में परञ्जोति की तलवार और उनकी शिव-सेवा एक ही हो गई।

panels.shot: wide aftermath shot inside Vatapi, streets half-ruined but calm
panels.action: Within Vatapi’s inner quarter, Paranjothi walks a street lined with damaged houses and closed doorways, a few Pallava soldiers clearing debris while smoke from small cooking fires signals life resuming.

dialogue.text: The city fell. Chronicles do not linger on cries and ruin, but we know that victory left shattered stone and shifted rule. The Pallava campaign reached its goal at Vatapi.

i18n.hi: नगर गिर गया। आख्यान चीखों और उजाड़ पर ठहरते नहीं, पर हम जानते हैं कि विजय ने पत्थर तोड़े और राज बदला। पल्लव अभियान वातापि में अपने लक्ष्य तक पहुँचा।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a Chalukya shrine space, solemn
panels.action: Paranjothi stands in a dim pillared chamber of a temple, looking at a squat, elegant stone image of Ganapati on a worn pedestal, its form rounded, trunk gently curving, lamps extinguished around it.

dialogue.text: Later tradition speaks of a Ganapati from Vatapi, carried away as a sacred trophy. Whatever its exact path, the story remembers a god-image crossing from a defeated capital to a new home.

i18n.hi: बाद की परम्परा वातापि के एक गणपति की बात करती है, जिसे पवित्र विजय-चिह्न बनाकर ले जाया गया। राह चाहे कैसी रही हो, कथा याद रखती है कि देव-मूर्ति हारी राजधानी से नए घर पहुँची।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Paranjothi’s hands respectfully lifting the image
panels.action: In a careful, reverent pose, Paranjothi bends and cradles the stone Ganapati in his arms, muscles tensed with its weight, his face lowered in concentration and quiet respect as temple shadows frame him.

dialogue.text: For warriors, spoils could be gold, land, captives. But here memory chooses a different centre: a commander lifting an image, not to desecrate it, but to carry it into his own world of worship.

i18n.hi: योद्धाओं के लिए लूट सोना, ज़मीन, बंदी हो सकती थी। पर यहाँ स्मृति दूसरा धुरा चुनती है: सेनापति एक मूर्ति उठाता है, उसे तोड़ने नहीं, अपनी पूजा की दुनिया में लाने को।

panels.shot: wide shot of homeward march, Ganapati image borne with care
panels.action: On the return journey across rolling dry fields, Paranjothi rides beside a cart on which the Ganapati rests cushioned; he walks alongside it for a moment, hand lightly touching the pedestal in silent vow.

dialogue.text: So the tradition of Vatapi Ganapati remembers return, not only conquest. A god of obstacle-removal, taken from Chalukya ground to Tamil soil, became a sign of power wrapped in devotion.

i18n.hi: इस तरह वातापि गणपति की परम्परा केवल विजय नहीं, वापसी भी याद रखती है। विघ्नहर्ता देवता, चालुक्य भूमि से तमिल धरती पर लाए गए, शक्ति और भक्ति की एक-साथ निशानी बने।

panels.shot: intimate wide of rural Tiruchengattankudy temple courtyard
panels.action: Paranjothi stands within a modest shrine complex at Tiruchengattankudy, trees shading the courtyard, villagers watching quietly as he oversees the careful placing of the Ganapati in a prepared sanctum niche.

dialogue.text: At Tiruchengattankudy in the Kaveri region, the Vatapi Ganapati tradition endures. It locates the image’s resting place not in a court temple of Kanchi, but amid fields, palms and village streets.

i18n.hi: कावेरी क्षेत्र के तिरुचेंगट्टनकुडी में वातापि गणपति की परम्परा आज भी है। वह मूर्ति का विश्राम-स्थान कांची के राज-मंदिर में नहीं, खेतों, खजूरों और गाँव की गलियों के बीच रखती है।

panels.shot: medium shot, frontal, Paranjothi before the newly installed Ganapati
panels.action: Paranjothi kneels on stone before the Ganapati now adorned with simple flowers, his sword and helmet set aside behind him, palms joined, eyes closed in long, steady prayer.

dialogue.text: This act of enshrining is central. A man who wielded troops now offered service in ritual, setting down his weapons and bowing to a god carried from the echo of siege into village quiet.

i18n.hi: यह प्रतिष्ठा का काम मुख्य है। जो आदमी सेनाएँ चलाता था, अब अनुष्ठान में सेवा देता है, हथियार रखकर उस देव को झुकता है जिसे घेरे से उठाकर गाँव की शांति में लाया गया।

panels.shot: close-up on Paranjothi’s thoughtful face lit by lamp glow
panels.action: In the dim inner shrine, Paranjothi’s face is half-lit by the warm glow of a single oil lamp, features softened, his expression moving from stern resolve to a quieter, inward steadiness.

dialogue.speaker: paranjothi_siruthondar
dialogue.text: Let my discipline serve not only kings, but the Lord who witnesses all.

i18n.hi: मेरी अनुशासन केवल राजाओं नहीं, उस प्रभु की भी सेवा करे जो सब देखता है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of temple street across years, same vantage
panels.action: The viewpoint shows the temple street over implied years: Paranjothi aged slightly, now in simpler cloth beside brahmins, farmers, women and laborers, all sharing space in processions and daily worship.

dialogue.text: Bhakti was remaking society. Warriors, farmers, merchants, women and marginalized devotees all entered shared songs and stories, bound not by rank but by their love for Siva and other deities.

i18n.hi: भक्ति समाज को नया रूप दे रही थी। योद्धा, किसान, व्यापारी, स्त्रियाँ और हाशिए के भक्त सब साझा गीतों-कथाओं में जुड़े, दर्जे से नहीं, शिव व अन्य देवों के प्रेम से बंधे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Paranjothi listening to Tamil hymns sung in the temple
panels.action: Paranjothi stands near a temple pillar as a small group chants Tamil Shaiva hymns; he listens intently, head bowed, fingers resting lightly on prayer beads, absorbed in the cadence of the verses.

dialogue.text: Sundarar’s Tiruthonda Thogai would later name a Siruthondar among Siva’s devotees, a warrior remembered for devoted service rather than for killing, counted in sacred company by song.

i18n.hi: सुन्दरर की तिरुथोंडा थोगै में बाद में सिरुथोंदार का नाम शिव-भक्तों में आता है, वह योद्धा जो हत्या नहीं, सेवाभाव से याद रखा गया, गीत में पवित्र संगति में गिना गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscriptional-style stone wall with imagined names
panels.action: A carved stone wall fills the frame, with neat rows of Tamil script; in the foreground Paranjothi touches the wall gently, while behind him ordinary worshippers move, their forms blurred.

dialogue.text: Between inscription and hymn, history and memory speak differently. Inscriptions recall kings and campaigns; hymns remember those who served Siva, weaving warriors like Siruthondar into devotional lineage.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख और स्तुति के बीच इतिहास और स्मृति अलग बोलते हैं। शिलालेख राजाओं और अभियानों को याद रखते हैं; भजन उन लोगों को जो शिव की सेवा में लगे, सिरुथोंदार जैसे योद्धाओं को भक्ति-वंश में बुनते हैं।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of Paranjothi alone on riverbank at dusk
panels.action: Paranjothi sits on a stone by a broad river at dusk, his cloak wrapped loosely, sword no longer at his side, watching the water’s slow flow while temple towers silhouette the far bank.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, hagiographers would build legends around Siruthondar, adding miracles and extreme tests. Scholars remind us these are later adornments, not firm record, colored by devotion’s imagination.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद पुराण-लेखक सिरुथोंदार पर चमत्कारों और कठोर परीक्षाओं की कथाएँ सजाने लगे। विद्वान बताते हैं कि ये बाद की सजावटें हैं, पक्के इतिहास नहीं, भक्ति की कल्पना से रंगी।

panels.shot: medium shot, Paranjothi offering food humbly to visiting ascetic
panels.action: In a simple courtyard, Paranjothi, now plainly dressed, serves a meal to a visiting Shaiva ascetic seated on a mat, his posture low and respectful, echoing disciplined service in everyday kindness.

dialogue.text: The core truth is quieter: service can shift from field to hearth, from war-camp to shrine, without losing its discipline. The same trained will can protect, can provide, can bow.

i18n.hi: मूल सच शांत है: सेवा खेत से चूल्हे, युद्ध-शिविर से मंदिर तक बदल सकती है, बिना अपना अनुशासन खोए। वही अभ्यासित इच्छा रक्षा भी कर सकती है, पालन भी, प्रणाम भी।

panels.shot: final wide shot inside Tiruchengattankudy temple, focus on Ganapati
panels.action: Inside the Tiruchengattankudy sanctum, the Vatapi Ganapati sits adorned with garlands and lamps; behind the soft haze of incense, Paranjothi’s figure is faint, half-merged with generations of worshippers.

dialogue.text: Today Vatapi Ganapati still receives flowers, and Siruthondar rests in Shaiva memory as a warrior-devotee. Through him we see how devotion welcomed every calling, turning history’s iron into song.

i18n.hi: आज भी वातापि गणपति फूल स्वीकार करता है, और सिरुथोंदार शैव स्मृति में योद्धा-भक्त के रूप में विश्राम करता है। उसके ज़रिए दिखता है कि भक्ति हर काम को अपनाती है, इतिहास के लोहे को गीत में गलाकर।

title_i18n.hi: परञ्जोति घर ले जाता है वातापि गणपति को

subtitle_i18n.en: Warrior of Vatapi, Servant of Siva
subtitle_i18n.hi: वातापि का योद्धा, शिव का सेवक
